How to use this very large guide

P1To make it easier, you can begin with the Quick start section, then learn one of the inductions and the whole return sequence. Then, you can read the Let the next response guide you section, for the part of the practice no recording can decide in advance. You can also look at the daily and weekly sections to make the practice your own. There are lots of appendices with extra tools, covering lots of topics, including asking questions, NLP patterns of language, working with anxiety, working with daydreams, altered states in general, what to do if you experience the sensation of a hostile presence, working with sleep, influence, and more inductions. All sources used are in Appendix K.

Introduction

P1Hello Lovey Bunny!

P2Have you ever realized that you were born with an incredible brain/mind that has many layers of consciousness: dream, protect, analyze, imitate, love, remember, hide, show, heal, etc, etc?

P3Yet no one taught those layers to talk to each other, instead you were taught (or you figured out) that the way to ‘grow up’ and be an ‘adult’ is to push through, repress, suppress, pretend you’re confident, follow authority, go against authority, etc etc etc, and mind you deeper mind is still running all of the programs it’s running: child mind, guard mind (childhood protector parts, the protective reactions learned as a child), body mind, intuitive mind, fantasy mind (trying to become guidance mind), etc etc

P4While a lot of the teachings on hypnosis talk about the ‘subconscious mind’ like it’s one giant machine you just have to put the right commands into in order to get it to do what you want, for me, the most useful thing to do is sit and listen to the different parts of myself until they can all be heard.

P5I teach a self-hypnosis method that allows you to gather all of your attention and have your conscious mind, subconscious mind, body mind, inner child mind, protector part minds, adult mind and Higher Self be able to all hear and talk to each other.

P6“How do I do this?” you ask. Just listen. When you warm up to what’s there, protect it, clarify what it is, reality test it, and then act on it, you’ll find that you don’t even need to have a dramatic ‘trance experience’ to demonstrate the results of all parts of your mind talking to each other and trusting each other more.

P7I like to think of it like a ‘communion’ between all parts of our mind, where the conscious mind doesn’t have to shout from the roof top and the subconscious mind doesn’t have to manifest symptoms, dreams, cravings, day dreams and weird body signals in order to communicate.

P8I work with the subconscious as if it were a ecology, and often begin hypnosis working with the Higher Self (universal heart) and only separate into parts when needed. I combine this with inner child reparenting (a clever suggestion won’t heal a hurt young part), and also aspects of prompt engineering, as well as helping people to be literate in the domain of what’s hypnotizing them.

Quick start: do this first

P1To work on difficulties or cultivate positive qualities (love, curiosity, play, confidence, etc.), simply do these steps, in order: 1) Attention; 2) Notice; 3) Offer one fitting response; 4) Wait; 5) Come all the way back . Not much needs to happen in each session!

TY-6Spaces before a full stop or comma (22 places)Not approved yet
How Quick start: do this first, P1 would read
To work on difficulties or cultivate positive qualities (love, curiosity, play, confidence, etc.), simply do these steps, in order: 1) Attention; 2) Notice; 3) Offer one fitting response; 4) Wait; 5) Come all the way back . Not much needs to happen in each session!
How When the adult role is not available yet, P7 would read
This is a borrowed figure, so you’re still making the choice. The longer version of this exercise can be found in my Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide .
How Before you begin, P4 would read
Deciding to do it . How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? Something else? Preview what you are going to do: will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are going to use a recording, read the script if you can. Know that you can say stop at any time and the induction will end. If you want to change something, say less if you want it to be asking for less from you, or quiet and the talking will stop. You can also just open your eyes and stop, and then come all the way back anyway. You don't need to ask any parts for permission to stop, even if a part tells you that you do.
How Before you begin, P6 would read
Let your response guide you as to what to do next regardless of what the script is expecting. Utilize. Use what you have to go to the next place, whatever it is. Learn how to notice what is there. Learn how to notice if there is no change, and that that is not a positive change. For more on language you can use, see Appendix B, or keep reading below for information on using the tools after induction in Let the next response guide you . Either way, keep the instructions about how to stay safe and how to get out plain.
How Finish without forcing a revelation, P1 would read
Ending the session . Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a ‘great revelation’! When you have done as much as you want to do, it is a good idea to find out if there is anything that you need to do to make sure that you can leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something ‘in real life’ (eat a good meal, put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc) or it may be that there is nothing to do!
How Installing the synchronicity cue, P10 would read
This is very similar to implementation intention . I'm not aware of research into implementation intention for this specific thing, but the general mechanisms appear to work; Gollwitzer’s paper explains how and why they work.
How Somatic Experiencing, P1 would read
Somatic experiencing: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide . In somatic experiencing (SE), you are not thrusting into the trauma. You learn to track. So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.
How Learning, entering, and returning, P2 would read
Healing the Divided Self , Maggie Phillips and Claire Frederick, (1995) pp 24-27, 45-50, 83-90, covers a lot of aspects of this post, such as interactive hypnosis, helping the subject learn how to learn by using other senses, learning self hypnosis, making sure the subject comes back at the end, etc. However, this is a professional clinical book, not a self help book, so be careful about trying to use the procedures used with the cases, etc in this book for solo work (the same applies to historical information it contains). Also, Adam Eason's work with Benjamin Parris in the International Society of Hypnosis, specifically his article about self hypnosis , should be a useful thing to read (especially the parts that talk about how to learn to learn when you're directing it yourself, and about whether you need another person to help you, and using recordings to help you, etc.)
How Indirect language and re-entry cues, P1 would read
For information about using indirect hypnotic language patterns, such as pacing, utilizing, metaphor, and associational cues, etc, see Healing the Divided Self , Phillips and Frederick, 1995, pp 53 - 57, 96 - 100, as well as nimja's tutorial on hypnotic language patterns , and his tutorial on triggers . The information on these techniques comes from these sources, not because they are necessarily validating the validity of some aspects of NLP, or because every example suits trauma work (nimja did not write or endorse this guide), but because I was adapting the language used for my own purposes, and I deliberately used a sequence that would be easy to use for re-entry.
How Body awareness and changing the amount of contact, P1 would read
NOTE: Some of the information in this post comes from In an Unspoken Voice , Peter Levine, 2010, especially ch 5 and 7, as well as ch 3 and 4 of Freedom from Pain , Levine and Maggie Phillips 2012, and ch 4 of Healing Trauma , by Levine. These sources talk about the key concepts of tracking what is happening in the body, resources, titration, pendulation, and the range of foci available when working, from sensation and imagery to behavior, emotions, and meaning, etc. This is not done from a position of "here is what you need to do to physiologically fix it", but here are some things you can try, etc.
How Inner-child care and adult capacities, P1 would read
For information about all of these things, see Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide . The practices in this post are designed to match with those in the guide, but include some elements of learning to get into self hypnosis, as well as other helpful language, and making sure you come back at the end, etc.
How Inner-child care and adult capacities, P2 would read
Some of the information in this post is taken from Healing the Divided Self , Phillips and Frederick, 1995, pp 148-153, 171-174, about renurturing work, and how it can be combined with somatic work, and how to develop capacities for nurturing, etc. For information about attunement, and how every child is different and needs to be responded to differently, see Trauma Through a Child's Eyes , Levine and Maggie Kline, especially ch 4, 5, 10, etc, as it talks about actual kids (and this guide is applying this to how to respond to younger feeling states within an adult). The sequence for doing this with borrowed adulthood and the arrangement of 3 functions of adulthood, etc, is not from these authors, however.
How Inner speech and putting experience into words, P1 would read
Not everybody has an inner voice , Nedergaard and Lupyan 2024, is not about self hypnosis adaptations, but about people with different amounts of inner speech. The questions in the quick start are not a validated way of seeing if you can do self hypnosis, but are simply there as a practical way of seeing for yourself how you are.
How Memory, support, and choosing a practitioner, P1 would read
Chapter 7 of Trauma and Memory , by Peter Levine, 2015, contains useful information on this. This US Veterans Administration website , contains useful general information about hypnosis, such as the fact that it can be very strong and should be carefully used, and that it may result in false memories. This ASCH website , contains information about the usefulness of getting certified in hypnosis, and why it doesn't guarantee competence. Links are available for these and other useful groups in the evidence and specialist sections, but they point to their particular claims, not every use of hypnosis.

Do you usually think in words?

P3If you don't normally think in words, you may want to say things aloud, in writing, on a recording, etc., when this guide says "say." Or, just do what it invites, without preparing what you're going to say. When it says "ask" the child or protector, or "listen" for a response, it doesn't mean they'll be saying full sentences to you. It also doesn't mean you'll get pictures in your head instead. Just do whatever you can, and try different ways as needed.

What I mean by hypnosis

P1APA Division 30 commonly defines hypnosis as focused attention, reduced peripheral awareness, and increased responsiveness to suggestion. That’s basically true, but there’s a lot more than meets the eye. In fact, hypnosis is such a broad and common type of altered state that it’s hard to confine it to one use. But I’m using hypnosis here as a therapy.

P2And hypnosis as a therapy is as old as time itself. While the modern technique of it was discovered by Franz Anton Mesmer in the 1770s, shamans have been using dancing, music, and drugs to induce hypnosis for therapeutic purposes forever. We enter into trance states every night which resemble hypnosis as we go to sleep and as we wake up as well. Those states can also be used for deep therapy.

Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists

P1Hypnotism can happen in a therapist’s office, but it can also happen through music, marketing, religious rituals, sexual chemistry, charismatic authority, social media, grief, fear, political messaging, sense of belonging, fatigue, love, trauma, beauty, etc.

P2Even when not actively engaging the conscious mind, there are many ways to influence people. Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well. In the Federal Trade Commission’s report on “dark patterns,” they describe designs that trick or manipulate consumers. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) describes commercial patterns that steer, deceive, coerce, or manipulate people toward choices that may work against their interests.

P3Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent. Can people have their minds influenced without conscious agreement of their adult self?

P4As associated with the Silva “Mind Control” method:

P5“If you don’t learn to control your mind, someone else will!”

P6As you're certainly aware there are many, many forces at work in the world that are already training your mind. With self-hypnosis you can do much of the same thing from the inside, by befriending and listening to the deeper part of your mind. This opens up a whole new area of choice for you as an adult in the world.

Affirmations Done Right

P1My dad always said: “Always, and in everything, expect the very best. But be prepared to take what you get. The best might come afterwards.” That’s a better affirmation than what most people think of as affirmation, because it’s not telling you something which you know to be false in the present. If you say “I am beautiful” but you know that’s not true, then you’re challenging your beliefs, and if you’re challenging your beliefs you should have some argument or reason why they are wrong, otherwise it’s bullying.

P2Another quote I use all the time from my dad… when someone asks me “How’s it going?” I say “Better & better!” This really confuses a lot of people. Some think it’s amazing that I’m always doing better. Some ask if I was sick or something. But it’s doing multiple jobs. On the one hand, it’s deflecting from the fake question because most people don’t actually want to hear how you are doing in detail anyway. On the other hand, more importantly, it’s reprogramming your mind to remove you from tunnel vision. You might be sad now, but if you say, “I am sad” then you’re subtly identifying with the sadness and it keeps you stuck. It’s best to say, “I’m feeling sad now, but I’m doing better and better, every day, in every way!” That’s more like a mission statement than a historical analysis. Although you can also re-evaluate your history as lessons to make that true.

P3Try it out right now and see how it feels!

Reversing Accidental Affirmations

P1Many times, we say things that we wish we hadn’t said, or our minds wander into places that we actually don’t want to live in. A very common example is masturbation, where people might fantasize about someone they don’t really want to be with in real life. While it might be optimal to just avoid doing that, if it does happen, it’s good to apply a trick my sister taught me, which she learned from Positive Magic. Right after the wrong thought, say, “I take it out of the law of cause and effect.” It’s not exactly magic, and it’s not like you can actually remove anything from laws of nature, but it does sort of do that because without the rupture in your thought stream, you can end up just going directly where it leads you. With the intentional correction, you don’t have to be unconsciously led astray but your random wrong thoughts.

Hypnosis Evidence

P1Is there REAL (not magical) evidence for Hypnosis? Yes. In 2024 there has been an overview of 49 meta analyses containing a total of 261 distinct primary studies. Evidence was strongest for pain, medical procedures, and work with children and adolescents, but varied with different outcomes and study design quality.

P2Is there evidence for Self-Hypnosis? Yes. There has been a systematic review of Randomized Controlled Trials of self-hypnosis, finding benefit in studies of pain, child birth, pediatric, stress, anxiety etc. Self-hypnosis seemed more useful when done as a real self-skill several times, not just listening to an audio file.

P3Here I will be teaching you a real self-skill, so you don’t end up a consumer of more and more elaborate trance recordings.

P5And it’s got to lead somewhere!

Why doing it myself worked better for me

P1Doing self-hypnosis on my own seems far more useful than the very little I managed to do with a professional hypnotist. I was sober at the session and didn't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me. The bigger issue was trust and precision.

P2When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using for a suggestion to my subconscious is slightly off, and talk to my subconscious to find out what it thinks is wrong with the wording. When I use an image, I can tell whether it's giving me useful information, or just telling me what I'm afraid of, or what I want to avoid, or what I want to be true, or something I don't understand yet. And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes.

P3A hypnotist working on me can't interact with my subconscious mind quickly enough to get the detailed feedback needed to know what's going on in my mind, since they aren't IN my mind. (Of course, there are advantages to having a skilled guide, since they may be able to see things I'm blind to, and can help me keep the process regulated and safe.)

P10Without drugs, self hypnosis or meditation might also work way better inside a lucid dream - I explain that possibility in my lucid dreaming guide.

A useful map of the mind

P1Note: whenever I refer to the ‘subconscious’ I’m referring to all of the processes under the surface of your conscious awareness: perceptions, emotions, desires, avoidance tendencies, imagery, memories, body signals, habits, intuitions, automatic behaviors and so forth. You can work with all of these together as if it’s all one ‘mind’, or you can work with it as a set of parts, an ‘ecology’ if you like. There isn’t a ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ way to approach it. They’re all maps. Don’t form a priesthood around either one!

P2Working with parts: Precision. Working with Higher Self: Coherence. Doing both: Communion.

P3If you need to work with the ‘whole’, the subconscious as one:

P4a) ‘Invoke’ the subconscious in some way. Something simple like ‘Hello, wise subconscious, please help me understand…’ or whatever works for you.

P5If you need to work with the ‘ecology’ in the subconscious (child parts, protectors, ‘critic’, fantasy making parts, body memories, social part, spiritual part (God/source/best benefit of all beings part) ‘wiser’ part etc etc then:

P6a) It’s usually a good idea to start with unity. So ‘invoke’ your Higher Self: Hello my Higher Self/universal heart-mind/wise subconscious, please guide me…

P7b) Move into differentiation. “Which part is afraid? Which part wants to protect you? Which part wants to avoid it? Which part knows what to do? Which part is too young for this?” Etc.

P8c) Move back into unity again. “And all of these parts are part of the one life, and as the adult in charge of this life you can lead with love…” Etc.

Sometimes start with the whole

P1Some people make themselves too fragmented by starting to work with parts. ‘Here’s a part! Here’s another one! I’ll get twelve of them in a room and give them all an office to hang around in!’ So it’s better to start from the Sacred.

P2Start like this: ‘I’m approaching this from the universal heart. I’m approaching this from my Higher Self. I’m approaching this from the part of me that knows it belongs to life, not any wound, or role, or family, or group, or identity, or ideology, or story. So can you please tell me what’s going to be true and kind and timely and stabilizing and useful here?’ Etc.

P3It can be that you can’t even access your Higher Self, or the universal heart, or whatever works for you. (Btw, if it doesn’t work for you don’t use it! It’s no good adopting somebody else’s map.) In that case, start by just witnessing whatever is coming up. Notice the room, your body, the fact that you’re in a younger state etc. Being able to notice is enough adult presence for the first step.

The inner child, the guards, and the inner adult’s three jobs

P1Your inner child won’t trust you right away. It’s not going to be enough for you to meditate, say three nice sentences to the inner child and expect to have its trust. What’s going to help your inner child to trust you is you, the person you are right now, becoming reliable.

P2Here I’m going to talk about what you develop in yourself as you reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three aspects: your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide, but I don’t mean them as if there were really three people in you. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.

When the adult role is not available yet

P1The problem is, that some people do not have access to their adult functions at will. Instead, they may go blank, access an inherited inner critic, or feel like a child part who may be playing at being an adult (what I call forced adulthood). Telling them to just access their adult is like telling a baby bird to just fly.

P2For that starting point, I have developed a kind of provisional bridge that I call “borrowed adulthood.” It is important to note here that I’m not suggesting that all of the steps in this process have been formally tested and proven.

P3Access your witnessing position if necessary, just noticing what’s there, without needing it to be warm or wise or certain. If you already know how to access different internal positions, move immediately to accessing the adult position you want to borrow.

P4If you have a safe adult in your life you can borrow from them, if not borrow from a mentor, older brother/sister, imagine your future self, your god/goddess or higher power, a value you have, a plan you have written, etc. It’s ok to just borrow what you need right now, warmth or a boundary or direction, just like you would borrow a cup of sugar from a neighbor.

P5Next, put on your adult hat as if you are an apprentice adult and do or say what you think you should do or say. You should do at least part of what you think you should do or say.

P6•Return the adult hat, noticing what you borrowed and what you were able to do on your own (even if it’s only 5%).

P7This is a borrowed figure, so you’re still making the choice. The longer version of this exercise can be found in my Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide .

P8You don’t have to have trustworthy people in your history. Use someone you remember when that helps, or just imagine a good adult whose intention is to take good care of you. See if you can imagine what they would say/do in your situation, with your history, limitations, options, etc. If you can’t imagine good, start with the least cruel response you can believe. Once you’ve found something good, try it, don’t keep doing the exercise.

The two-hand practice

P1There is a simple and easy body technique to connect with your inner child. Just place one hand in the center of your chest which is physically connecting you to your love and then place your other hand just below that which is your solar plexus and where your child can be.

P2Begin to send love from your heart down to your child and just notice what comes up for you. It doesn't matter if something comes up or not. If you feel resistance, just meet it with love. If you feel or see something, just meet that with love as well. This is a conversation with your child from your heart.

The Nurturer

P1The Nurturer: Some of the work you can do as the Nurturer is to enjoy your inner child. You don't have to move their feelings, just sit back and enjoy them. Be happy that they are there. Children need to be enjoyed! Say things to your inner child like:

P2It's okay to feel the way you're feeling.

P3I want you to know that I'm here for you.

P4You don't need to do anything right now.

P5It's okay. You're not too much. You can be small here.

P6You can be angry here.

P7You can be sad here.

The Protector

P1As the Protector, work with setting boundaries together. They can be simple like, "I'm going to leave this conversation because it's not safe" or "I'm going to stop texting the person who destabilizes me." It can be self-care boundaries like, "I'm going to eat" or "I'm going to get some sleep." It can be trust-related boundaries like, "I'm going to keep the promise to myself" or "I'm not going to leave you to do adult things by yourself."

Working with childhood protector parts

P1Working with childhood protector parts:

P2Feel free to use parts language here, too, if it’s helpful. Often, we see a sensation or a distraction or an objection as something that needs to be explored, when in fact it might just be hunger, or reasonable skepticism about something, or a sentence that doesn’t fit. It’s good to notice it, though, and then to see what might be going on.

P3If you're not careful, you might find yourself expecting that when you go within to meet your inner child, you'll find your inner child.

P4Instead, you might feel numb, cynical, angry, hungry, like you need to look at your phone, sexually aroused, like you need to make plans, sleepy, dissociated, or you might even think that what you're doing is stupid. Those are not failures, they are you experiencing what is often a very charming guard, a childhood protector part. It's what protects you when your consciously installed parental Protector isn't functioning, the same as when you were a child.

Moves (ST-3.2)

P5One important thing to become aware of when approaching your inner child is your inherited parent script. This is the set of rules and ways of treating yourself that you internalized as a child, mostly based on how your parent(s) treated you, and it doesn’t always sound like a voice. This is not the same as your inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Guide) that you build up on purpose. Often this script acts as a critic or warden, telling your inner child not to cry, not to be “needy”, not to embarrass them, not to be too independent, etc. So when you begin talking to your child in a new, loving way, the script may jump in to say that what you’re doing is “fake”.

When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice

P1It can be difficult to connect with your inner child if your inner child didn’t have the opportunity to develop. This happens often when you grow up in a situation where you don’t have a private self, for example when your family, religion, or community ‘takes over’ very early in your life. Or you are pushed to achieve very early in life. The result is that you don’t know what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like and dislike until you have heard someone else’s opinion about it. If you are in that situation, it can be difficult to follow the advice to ‘love yourself’. You don’t even know who ‘yourself’ is! So you can do reparenting and finding yourself in parallel. For others, it is very easy to work with the inner child, they can feel it easily.

De-hypnosis: wake up inside the influence

P1One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is that sudden "waking up" to all the ways your attention is being shaped in your day-to-day life. There are actually multiple patents on using screens to send subliminal messages, but even without that kind of potentially illegal tech, the screen is one connection to the omnipotent Algorithm. Which shows us ads and guides our preferences. Then we wonder why we vote for this or that politician. But there are also the older, more mundane influences: erotic imprinting (as if breast implants are actually sexy), religious fear, which tags along with shame, charismatic authority and pressure to belong. And all of that drilled repeatedly into us, because one exposure won't do the trick. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.

Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

P1Inductions serve to gather you up so you can access quiet stuff. They're not about surrendering or playing asleep or obeying someone. Sometimes it's nice to do an actual induction if you're sober but distracted or analytical or otherwise not very trancey. If on the other hand, you're already pretty trancey for whatever reason (meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, tired, whatever...), skip straight to the orientation/containment part rather than going deeper.

What an induction is actually doing

P1Getting yourself ready to do something. Part of that is gathering your attention up. Part of that might be deepening. Part of that is letting what you notice inform the words you're hearing and what you do next. There are lots of different ways to do this. For this method, I'm going to be counting, but you could do all sorts of things. If you want to just talk, or tell a story, or move, or make sounds, or be curious, or whatever, by all means, just do that. The only thing is, say that you're doing it. Don't pretend you're doing something else, in the name of elegance or whatever.

P2Test: Are you getting the response you want out of this already? If so, you might not need to deepen.

Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

P1Keep it simple. One thing you're doing, one anchor/image you're going with at first, one way of coming back, and feel free to set a tone (warm, bounded, directed, neutral witnessing, whatever) for yourself. If you're going to use metaphors (you don't have to) just do one, and if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that's conscious.

P2Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional. You can use whatever form of signal makes sense to you (feelings, rhythms, movements, words, spatial, simple knowing, lack of signal, whatever) but if you're using words, try to keep them related to whatever world you're creating. If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world. And when you're done, come back the other way. (You can borrow qualities, but don't change who you are.)

P3When you're writing this, think about what the verb you're using is, what the sensory quality is, what the short refrains are, and how you're going to transition between ideas. Read it out loud as you're writing it. Long, elegant sentences don't read well when you're being induced. It's all just soup.

Before you begin

P11.Read this page, and the Come all the way back page, when you're awake.
P22.Get clear on what it is you want to do during the induction. What do you want not to do today. How long do you want to spend on this? (You don't have to do this on a problem. You can do it on something you want to experience more of: love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, whatever.) Make sure you're leaving some time at the end to come back, and reflect on what you experienced.
P33.Put yourself in a place where you can safely do this. Don't do this if you're driving, in the water, operating machinery, or otherwise need to be attending to yourself or other people. If you are overwhelmed by chemicals, acutely confused, or not able to keep yourself safe, then get some immediate support instead of doing exploratory hypnosis. (The later part of this can be used to help orient you if you're already open, but don't use it to make yourself deeper if you're not stable.)

P3You can allow yourself to notice something you can feel, like the sensation of something under you, and notice the sensation of the contact, the pressure. Or maybe there is a sound, or something else to notice.

P4Allow yourself some time to do this.

P5You might notice yourself thinking, and whenever you notice yourself thinking, you can allow yourself to re-engage with your anchor and leave the thought unfinished.

P6You might notice something that you are doing that holds your interest, something about the sound, or sensation, or listening or something else.

P7Allow yourself some time to do this, as much time as you would for someone you care about who has started to talk and hasn't gotten to what she wants to say yet, so you are going to stick around till she gets it all out.

P8Repeat the phrase that you chose, if you want to. Say it as an invitation and notice how it's received.

P9You can close your eyes now if you want to. If not, it's fine to keep them open, or soften your gaze. The listening might go deeper while there's still a background sound you can hear.

P10Count 5 to 1, taking your time if you like.

P115.Let your attention come back to your chosen anchor. 4. Let more of your attention come to what you've found. 3. Leave a little space. 2. See if you can listen to a space after the words without preparing an answer. 1. Take your time.

P12Bring to mind, if you want, the thing that you want to talk about, or just the wish to have inner contact. Just let it be there for now. You don't need to tell the whole story yet.

P13What do you notice now?

P14Let yourself notice what comes to you, if anything. It may not be clear yet what it is. It may be sensations, words, pictures, feelings, movements, or anything else.

P15Let yourself take your time to notice, with or without words.

P3Say something like, "If I'm meant to be getting guidance, please show me the action I need to take. If I'm avoiding something, please bring me back to now and show me what I'm avoiding."

ST-5.2, new subheading: Turning the shortcut off, or keeping it

P8If you want to turn this one off, simply don't practice it anymore. Take it out of your recordings, take it out of your apps if you're using it in an app, and start using your regular induction. Come all the way back

P1If you have done anything to alter your state when coming out of a trance, make sure to reverse those things. If you have floated, make sure to gain your weight again (whatever weight you want of course). If you have shrunk, make sure to grow back to your regular size. If you have met a younger state or are working with parts, make sure to come back to feeling complete in your body in the here and now, that your body belongs to you, and that it is under control of your adult mind. If you have gone somewhere, make sure to go back the same way you went there. Etcetera. Make sure to only take with you when you come out of a session the things that you want to!

P3Then do a count up: On 1 start to feel your body again and what it's resting on and feel your weight (of your choice). On 2 start to feel your breathing return to normal. On 3 start to hear the room around you and name where you are. On 4 start to wiggle your fingers and toes, move your shoulders and your eyes. On 5 open your eyes, back in the here and now, feeling normal and clear and the session is now over.

P4When you come out make sure you can name what day (or date) it is, look to your left and right, look at something near to you and something further away. Move around a bit. Don't get up until you feel like you can do so without falling over. Make sure that you are oriented and alert (counting does this, but not always). Take mental note of only what actually came up for you and any actions you need to take regarding it. Then go on and do something normal.

The actual inner meeting

P1Note: If you have a tendency to day dream, dissociate or fall asleep, it is better to do this exercise sitting up and save lying down for when you want to go to sleep, get a very deep rest or incubate dreams. If you are sitting, keep your spine straight but not rigid like a soldier. Relax your jaw and stay somewhat connected to the room you are in.

P2“I am not leaving life; I am listening more deeply to life.

P3I invoke my Higher Self, universal heart-mind, wise subconscious mind, intelligence in my body, inner child(ren), inner adult(s), protector(s) and all that is of truth and love to help me know what I need to know in a form and at a level that will be useful, kind, stabilizing and real for me.”

P4Ask your conscious mind to listen.

P5This does not mean you have to stop thinking to listen. Just notice your thoughts, body sensations, pictures, doubts, emotions, etc. Don’t fight what comes up, but don’t go with it either. Just notice what stands out on its own as you hold the idea of what you are doing in the back of your mind.

P6Internally say, “Tell me what I need to know or ask me what you need to know and I’ll sit in silence for 5 minutes and listen.”

P7You may hear a phrase, feel a body sensation, notice a memory, see a color, be contacted by a child or protector, feel pain, warmth, complete silence, know that you need to do something, be grateful for something, feel you need to stop the listening or any number of things.

P8Listen to everything and believe nothing automatically.

P2Respond to each thing that comes up with an accurate notice and a small reasonable invitation (or act or taking more time etc). The 'thing' might be a sensation, image, gesture, feeling, words, or anything. The notice and invitation don't need to take all those forms, just notice and invite what happens.

Finding your own words

P1An example notice might be, "I notice my chest tightening when I imagine asking for help". Don't add interpretation like "this must be the abandoned child part of me, or a protective mechanism" - just notice what you notice. An example invitation might be, "And as I notice that, I can take some time before deciding what it means, and notice if I want to say anything, or change it, or just stay like that".

P2Then just listen. You don't need fancy language - often it will be better to just ask what happens next, or whatever. If you notice a feeling developing, it might be best not to say anything while it's developing (if you can help it) but some days you need to talk to understand, so just do that.

P3You can be pretty straightforward when that's the help you chose - "Let the explanation wait a moment. What do I feel as I say that?" can be a perfectly valid thing to say to yourself, and help you focus. It's ok to just be with an unpleasant feeling, you don't have to wait till it's a nice one before you know you're ok. As long as you're still present, and able to change if you want to, and happy to carry on, a sad feeling or tension or whatever doesn't mean it's not ok.

P2On the other hand, you may find that you have acted inappropriately and you feel guilty. Having feelings of guilt does not mean that you have done something wrong or that you have been manipulated. Have you done something that was wrong or that caused harm? If so, what can you do to fix it? On the other hand, did you give in to someone else just to keep them from being disappointed in you? What do you want to do or achieve the next time you interact with this person? Do you need them to understand what you are feeling/thinking? Do you just need to communicate information to them? Do you need to set boundaries with them? Do you need to end the interaction prematurely? You don’t have to make them understand before you can act.

Change the amount of contact

P1When you start to contact it, if it feels too much, immediately start to widen your awareness to something else in the room, in your body, etc. Keep moving back and forth between the difficult thing and the easier thing. This is called pendulation and titration. Do as much or as little as you feel you can. You set the pace, you don’t have to do a certain number.

Offer the care that is actually wanted

P1If any “younger” parts come up, offer them the opportunity to spend time with you, or some space if they would rather. If one of them says “don’t come closer”, stay at the distance they choose. If you can identify any “protector” parts, talk to them and find out what they are concerned about. All of them are welcome to the “meeting”. You don’t have to get rid of any of them.

P3Try some different ideas as to what might be helpful for this ‘inner part’ to feel better (being welcomed by you, visualizing someone else, giving them the sort of words they would like to hear, you placing yourself in a different body position, you moving further away etc). Only try one idea at a time to see if it works. Just because an idea ‘should’ be a resource, that doesn’t mean that it will be.

P4It is possible that when you try and give the part what it wants, you might feel very upset. It may be that it never got what it needed at the time and now that you are giving it what it wants, it is processing the upset of not getting what it wanted before. If this happens, allow yourself to respond for as long as you want to do so, and for as long as you can ‘stay there’ (ie remain in the process). If you feel that the voice, distance, touch, image etc is too much, then change it to something that is less. Don’t think that you can’t ‘take’ the love.

P5Allow yourself to see where the metaphor takes you. Ask questions like ‘if the problem had an image or story, what would it be?’ or ‘what would need to happen to make things right?’ If it feels like you need to ‘do something’ to give yourself the resource that you feel you need (or to put a boundary in place, or to move away or to take some other action) then try ‘doing that’ for as far as it takes to be of use to you. Remember that whatever you find out, is likely to be metaphorical. It may be a good hypothesis for what you need to do but it is not a proven fact.

P6Alternatively, you may want to use the session to develop a capacity that you want to develop (ie love, play, courage, curiosity etc). You can also use it to rehearse something that you have decided to do.

Finish without forcing a revelation

P1Ending the session . Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a ‘great revelation’! When you have done as much as you want to do, it is a good idea to find out if there is anything that you need to do to make sure that you can leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something ‘in real life’ (eat a good meal, put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc) or it may be that there is nothing to do!

The 15-minute daily practice

P1Notice there is no need to learn a second script! The process is the same. You are simply practicing for fifteen minutes or so (a convenient time, not a dose or a timetable). That is long enough to induce yourself (it only takes a few minutes), practice and let it unfold at its own pace (five minutes is plenty to see what happens when you simply sit in silence, listening, and you can interrupt yourself at any time to change direction if that feels better) and come out again (that takes a few minutes too).

The weekly deeper practice

P1It’s good to give this more time once or twice a week, when that’s useful. It doesn’t have to be very intense but it is good to start from Higher Self or at least a neutral witnessing place and follow what appears. It’s also good to bring in some adult function to make sure nothing is being bypassed and so that at the end of the exercise, when the experience is over, there is the possibility of coming out completely and doing whatever normal thing needs doing.

P2If possible, it’s good to do the normal thing immediately after the exercise, so that the subconscious sees that the adult heard and acted. Otherwise, the dishes won’t get done.

Capacity before content

P1NOTE: If it is medically unsafe or you are in a place of panic, sleep deprivation, nausea, deep destabilization, mania, psychosis like symptoms, feeling overwhelmed by chemicals etc. then first focus on stabilizing and then look for what your subconscious needs you to know! If it takes you destabilizing to know what your subconscious knows, it is not meant for you to know directly at this time! Focus on asking for capacity over content!

P2Sometimes, it feels like your subconscious knows something that your conscious self is not prepared to know. It may be something related to your sexuality, grief, trauma, family issues, betrayal, shame, vocation, a relationship, illness fears, spirituality, addiction, identity, moral issues etc.

P3What you DON’T want to do is bully your subconscious into telling you what it knows by saying things to yourself like:

P4“What is it you won’t tell me? What are you hiding? Tell me NOW! I am telling you to tell me!”

P5This can lead to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation etc. and can make your day SUCK! When you are flooded, it is much harder to access your adult capacities so focus on being able to regulate and getting support! Sometimes, it is better not to know what is not being said until your adult has the capacities to regulate, get support, be humble, etc. Just ask for what you need to know in a way that you CAN tolerate:

P6“What can you tell me, that will make my conscious self 5% better at knowing the thing you want to tell me?” “Can you tell me in symbolic form so I am not completely overwhelmed by the revelation?” “Can you tell me what I need to do to be safe, without actually telling me what it is”? “Do I need to know WHAT it is, or do I need to know that I need to get some support to have the capacity to know what it is, and who would be a good person to help me?” etc.

P7Instead, say to yourself something like this:

P8“Dear Wise Subconscious Mind, if there is something you know that my conscious self is not ready to know, please don’t break it open violently! Do what you can to make me able to know it in a way that is safe! Prepare me BEFORE you break it open! Ground me BEFORE you show me the memory! Support me BEFORE you make it intense! Give me one next action!” etc.

P9REMEMBER: Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal, especially if it relates to trauma and memory. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!

The subconscious will not answer

P1There may not be an answer. There may not be an answer that will help you. You may need to try asking a different question or you may just need to rest or finish your inner work for the day. If trust is actually a concern, you can try asking your subconscious “What would you need to know in order to trust me?” Some examples of answers might be “I need to know you will set boundaries” “I need to know you will do what you said you will do” “I need to know you won’t keep leaving” “I need to know you won’t think that knowing something means that you don’t need to do anything about it” etc.

The inner child will not appear

P1If you can figure out who the guard is, talk to it. If you can’t, just work with what you are aware of. You can say to the guard “You don’t have to let me in, just tell me what I need to do to make it safe”. Even if there isn’t a child part that you can talk to, you can work with whatever you are aware of. You can work on your preferences or something that you’re curious about or something that you’re willing to try as a beginner etc. and see how it goes. Work on developing a sense of who you are and reparent yourself as best you can.

You get anxious

P1Find out if the anxiety is bad enough that you want to decrease contact with it or if you can manage it and let it continue. If the anxiety is getting too bad, then you need to stop searching for content and help your body first, like the following:

P2-Where are your feet? Where are you sitting? Focus on your body, your breathing, and the room around you.

P3-Tell your Little parts and childhood protector parts that you’re there for your Little parts and that you recognize that your protector parts are trying to protect you and that you don’t need them to scream at you in order for you to know that something is wrong. Ask them if they need you to do something and if they do, ask them to show you one step at a time that you can do. If they don’t, then ask them to let your body calm down.

You dissociate or feel unreal

P1Open your eyes, move around, feel something textured, name 5 things that you can see, and end your work for the day.

You become grandiose

P1Go eat, go to sleep, do some chores, accept some humility, find somebody to disagree with you, etc.

P2What do you say to yourself in that moment? “If it’s really there, it’ll still be here after a good night’s sleep, some food, some time, etc, and some subsequent humility, feedback, etc, etc.”

You become too analytical

P1You’re being too analytical. “What if you didn’t try to improve it?” Put your hand on your heart, your other on your solar plexus, and say, “I don’t have to do this perfectly. I’m here for a relationship with something deeper than my surface mind.” “What can you do to make this a communion, not a performance?” Maybe it’s silence, resting, or doing something. Whatever it is, just do it.

You become too blissful or diffuse

P1You’re being too blissful, diffuse, etc. Bring it down to a more specific level. “What’s the smallest, most specific thing you can do to demonstrate the love you’re feeling?”

You want the hidden truth immediately

P1Don’t pry.

P2“Show me the capacity before the content.”

You keep daydreaming

P1You’re daydreaming. Sit up and open your eyes, and ask yourself, “What are you avoiding doing in the real world by doing this?”

You get stuck in spiritual bypass

P1“Where has divine love not yet descended into the wound?”

P2Maybe you had a profound opening that showed you how much more love and freedom is possible. Let that matter, but don’t demand that the child receive it on command. Maybe when you prayed it seemed like you were being abandoned and condemned. Maybe you felt betrayed by a spiritual teacher. It may be worth exploring these, but you might not want to do more of the same.

P3Sometimes it’s best to get some practical help while life still feels too small, and let yourself be curious about finding more happiness, without necessarily believing the explanation of how it’s going to work. Sometimes people have enough love and meaning to just live their lives, and trying to be spiritual doesn’t have to be another assignment.

You get stuck in endless processing

P1You may have a real wound that needs to be dealt with, but it’s possible you’re caught in a checking loop. Consider asking yourself “Will processing this again actually help me feel, understand, decide, or do something differently? Or is this a form of checking to see if I can get the reassurance that something is finally okay?” Sometimes, whether you’re grieving or doing your practice, it’s okay to cover the same ground again and again.

P2The best thing to do, though, if you notice you’re in a checking loop, is allow the thought to be there without engaging with it and get on with what you have chosen to do. You don’t have to have a meeting with every thought that pops into your head before you start your life. You don’t have to do any certain thing before you start your life.

P3What would the Guide choose to do now?

You keep using hypnosis but not changing life

P1You’re doing hypnosis over and over again without making changes in your life. Ask yourself, “What can I do to show my kid I’m for real?” Then go do it.

Methods to explore with a trained person present

P1If you want to deliberately do trauma-focused regression (going backwards in your memory or imagination to times when you were younger), or affect and somatic bridging (following associations from an emotional or somatic experience to find the origin of that experience, particularly if it was a traumatic experience you don't know about), or if you find that you're having substantial flashbacks or dissociative reactions, then you should do this with a trauma-informed clinician present. Make sure they're trained in the specific method you want to do. Ask any potential person what they would do and how they deal with uncertainty and unexpected reactions. Note that even if you work with a person, hypnosis is not a way of knowing what did or did not happen to you. (Both regression and affect/somatic bridging can also be used to find resources and do other things, of course.)

Appendix A: How to ask the subconscious a useful question

P1Your subconscious mind is NOT a large language model of AI. However, there is a bit of overlap in the way you can ask questions to both. So, if you know how to do prompt engineering for AI, this can be very useful to use it to help you be more present, honest, loving etc. On the other hand, you should NEVER use it to be more controlling.

P2To get as much precision as possible, you need to include the following in your prompt:

P3Role: Who or what are you talking to?

P4Context: Give some context so it knows what you’re talking about.

P5Intention: What do you want to change or accomplish?

P6Constraint: What do you need to do to make sure your asking is safe, true, kind etc.

P7Output: How do you want to receive the answer? As an image, phrase, sensation in your body, memory, action, question, symbol, silence, rest etc.

P8Evaluation: How are you going to evaluate the answer? How will you know if it’s true, kind, timely, stabilizing, specific, testable etc?

P9Iteration: Iterate by changing your prompt depending on what you get from reality as feedback.

P10Most importantly, you always need to make your prompt “safe” otherwise, the analytical part of your mind will “make up” an answer just so it fits with your prompt. I usually add the following to my prompt:

P11“If you need more time or the best and safest answer is silence, then I ask you to make my body go into a deeper state of comfortable rest. A peaceful silence would be a successful answer to my question.”

P12There is a very good chance there is no answer for your question because there is nothing happening. It might be that it’s not time yet, or that you need to go rest or do whatever you need to do.

Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

P1Appendix B - NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming)

P2You do not need to know this stuff to do it but if you want to freshen up on your skills in the art of working with imagery, body states, behavioral rehearsal, talking to yourself in effective sentences etc then it might be useful, when it helps the system listen. Using the techniques can be an easy way to fall into the trap of thinking that NLP is a bag of tricks rather than something that needs to be done with love and truth and contact and consent.

The four NLP layers

P1The four levels of NLP are:

P2Sensory Level of NLP: working with the form of an inner experience (where do you see or hear it, how far away, how big, how bright, how loud, how do you hold your body, where is the pressure etc.)

P3State Level of NLP: making useful states (warmth, adult presence, courage, love etc.) easier to get to.

P4Strategy level of NLP: practising a better response.

P5Language Level of NLP: pacing what is true; opening up people’s awareness; presuming you can do something safe; linking cause and effect; embedding invitations; asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative or grandiose language.

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

P1To do this we are going to use a model that’s called the Milton model. It’s all to do with sentence architecture. When we tell ourselves to ‘be better’, ‘relax now’, ‘stop feeling anxious’ or ‘trust me’ it doesn’t work, does it?

P2What we need to do is use indirect language to go around the part that wants to argue with us, so that we can actually get to where we want to get to.

P3So let’s start with something we know to be true, let’s take the pressure off, presume that we can only do a tiny bit and let’s invite one thing:

P4‘As my body begins to notice the sensation of the bed underneath it, it may be possible for it to begin to realize that it is not alone in carrying the burden of the day.’

P5We paced it; we opened up awareness; we validated the reason for the reaction; we presumed we could do it; we used a bridge word to make it easier and we invited one thing. We can then test this out with the body to see if it was possible.

Pattern 1: Pacing and leading — truth before suggestion

P1So how might we pace and lead in a way that works with anxiety?

P2It might go something like this: ‘It is completely true that the sensation of ________ (or the emotion of _____) is coming up for me. It makes complete sense that my system is trying to react and respond to that by wanting to do or think ________. Whilst that is completely true, there is another thing that is equally true, which is that my adult self is here, breathing in the room right now, and wanting to listen to what comes up for me next.’

P3Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite etc. is all you need to do.

P1Open up awareness by using ‘awareness’ verbs e.g. notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen to, allow, discover, remember, consider etc.

P2"Can I allow the system to show me the next thing to do, without showing me all the details of wounding that are involved?"

Pattern 8: Tag questions

P1Similarly, you can use 'tag' questions, like "isn't it?" or "can't it?" or "doesn't it?" or others, but be aware that these can get pretty 'oily' pretty quickly, so don't overdo it.

P2"Your body knows how to relax, doesn't it?"

Pattern 9: Nominalizations

P1Nominalizations are words like, 'healing', 'safety', 'trust', 'integration', 'communion', 'clarity', 'rest', etc. These are a bit vague, and sometimes that can be useful, because it allows the subconscious to fill in the blank with something very specific for that person.

P2"I can allow myself some safety, in whatever way my body knows how."

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

P1To 'Milton Model' is to open things up. To 'Meta Model' is to say "What do yo mean by that?" In order to be ethical with people, you need to do both.

P2"What do you mean specifically? According to who? Compared to what? Always? Never? What specifically would happen if you did? How do you know that? What evidence could you have that would change your mind?"

P3When people are starting to get stiff in their bodies, 'Milton' it. When you feel like you're losing touch with the truth of what's going on, 'Meta' it.

Sensory, state, and strategy tools

Submodalities — editing the form, not denying the truth

P1If someone's fear, craving, fantasy, belief, memory, whatever, has sensory properties in your experience (it has a place in your visual field, or sounds a certain way, or is heavy, or moving, or inside / outside your body, or something like that), you can work with those properties. If there are no sensory properties that you can notice, don't try to create any -- just don't use this tool!

P2How is this represented for you? Can you allow yourself to move that image back a couple of feet? Can you soften the edges of that image? Can you turn the volume down on that voice in your head? Etc.

P3"And I can allow myself to know that I am not deleting the message, just turning down the volume so that I am able to be present enough to hear what it is."

P4And, always ask the guard if it's ok to do this.

P5"Is it ok to move that image back a couple of feet and turn the volume down a bit, so that I can be present enough to hear what you need me to hear?"

Anchoring — giving the body a doorway back

P1There are many ways to do this. Put your hand on your heart, touch two fingers together, use a breath, a word, a particular body posture, smell, song, whatever. Feel something that you have got to in reality that you want to be able to get to easily when you need to. Do your anchor thing and say to yourself that this is available to you. Do make sure you do it when you have clearly got it. To get yourself back into a good hypnosis state easily, dont go for a peak state but for a good hypnotic state. See the main induction for a quick way to get back into hypnosis. Do make sure this is different from both your alert and calm cue and your synchronicity wake up cue.

Installing the synchronicity cue

P1How to install Synchronicity cues:

P2Mentally rehearse the following: Imagine that you have noticed a synchronicity that is obviously harmless.

P3Feel the "whoa" of stimulation that you just got from noticing it.

P4Use that stimulation to feel your feet, your body, your breathing, your room.

P5Reiterate to yourself that whenever you notice a synchronicity, it is just a bell that rings to wake you up, it is not proof for what you are interpreting from it.

P6Ask yourself: "What does my Nurturer think about this?", "What does my Protector think about this?", "What does my Guide think about this?"

P7Rehearse going back to a more grounded state and to a more wide view of the situation.

P8Rehearse yourself taking at least one action. Rehearse yourself waking up completely.

P9Mind the caveats! You must be the one authoring these. You must see them. You can always undo them. You must use them only to help you orient. They do not authorize you to make a decision. They are not proof for what your intuition is telling you. They do not stop you from hearing the message of your intuition if it is warning you about something. Other people can't use them to control your response.

P11A downside of synchronicity cues is that they can lead to false positives. Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

P1Reframes are dishonest when they make the problem into something that was good all along. Instead ask yourself: What else might be true? or What is this part trying to do for me? or How might my Nurturer reframe this? or How might my Protector reframe this? or How might my Guide reframe this? etc., etc.

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

P1Here is a rough outline of the NLP tools and techniques I use:

Somatic Experiencing

P1Somatic experiencing: If you would like more information about somatic experiencing, or even a free intro session, please see my somatic guide . In somatic experiencing (SE), you are not thrusting into the trauma. You learn to track. So you might start by tracking, by discovering where the activation is, where a neutral place is, and then whether you can move your attention from one to the other, very slowly, like a snail.

Gendlin Focusing

P1Gendlin Focusing: Focusing is another approach where you work with your body. You might say to yourself, “What is the felt sense of this whole anxiety?” Don’t answer with your head; let your body come up with a vague sense of the whole anxiety. Then ask, “What would this felt sense like me to know?” Try a word or a phrase and see how well it fits the felt sense. But also see if what the word or phrase says is true of the situation. The word may feel ok, but say something that doesn’t fit the situation, or vice versa. Use the words and the body to mutually correct one another.

Appendix E: Is the daydream helping or replacing your life?

P1Sometimes daydreaming is something that your subconscious mind is doing to help you. It is simulating an idea or event to help you digest grief or teach you something. The very act of daydreaming may be helping you to access your creativity or allowing your subconscious to show you a potential future. Sometimes your subconscious will show you things that you may be afraid of. Sometimes it will show you what you want.

P2Other times daydreaming may be taking you away from your life in a detrimental way. It may be that you are escaping reality and are addicted to fantasies rather than the real life. You may be dissociating or obsessing about romantic partners or escaping from being an adult.

P3How do you know which it is? Simply ask yourself if the daydreaming is taking you closer to life, with more clarity, love and ability to take action or if it is taking you away from life, in a repetitive and craving way.

P4If it is helping you then simply ask yourself what the guidance is and how you can use it.

P5If it is taking you away from life then change your body position by sitting upright, open your eyes, feel your feet and ask your subconscious to help you. Simply say to yourself, “Dear subconscious thank you for showing me images. If what you are showing me is helpful then please also show me the helpfulness in it. If what you are showing me is a way of avoiding dealing with life then please show me in a gentle but structured way how to deal with life as it is right now.”

P3That said, self hypnosis may be the best way of talking to your subconscious on a day to day basis. If you’re dealing with particularly complicated trauma, blind spots, dissociation, destabilization, or relational wounds that need another nervous system, skilled outside support may be best.

Finding a hypnotist who can work with you

P1What they are trained in (what they can treat) How they use hypnosis What they will do if things don't "fit" (if they are treating trauma, did they have specific training on trauma and dissociation? Having hypnosis certifications matters, but doesn't mean they are trained in trauma care)

P2What has/hasn't worked for you in the past How direct you want them to be What kind of touch (if any) you are ok with What kind of imagery (if any) you are ok with What you want them to do if you want them to stop What they will do if things go unexpected during or after the session What they do if you aren't sure if something is a memory or not How they will do the full return (coming out of hypnosis) at the end of the session You should be able to be firmly encouraged, but not forced to continue if you don't want to.

P3Then afterwards, check in about what was actually done, regardless of what you might call the method. Ask the person why they did what they did, if they told you in advance. Did you agree to it? How did the person respond to you? Keep in mind that just because something made you uncomfortable, it doesn't mean it was "bad," but if they saw your discomfort as meaning that you needed more of it, that might be something to look into. You might even be able to use this app or ask around to see if someone can tell you what the things they did meant. They probably won't be able to tell you if the person was "certified" in them or not, though. Then you can decide if you want to try learning to do self-hypnosis, using both, or find someone else. Those are all good options.

When the subconscious speaks like an oracle

P1Your subconscious is amazing at picking up on things your conscious mind isn't getting. Whether it's anticipations, reading patterns, or just picking up on uncanny things, it's good to respect what your subconscious is picking up on. But just because your subconscious gives you an image or tells you to do something, that doesn't mean you need to treat it like an order.

P2Especially if it's a big thing, or something that can't be easily undone, slow it down to the scale of the thing. Look at it with your adult's eyes, and take it to council.

The council — internal first, then outward

P1Ask your child, your adult, your conscious mind, your subconscious mind, your intuition, your analytical mind. But if it's bigger than all of those, ask outside of yourself, too. The bigger and more un-undoable something is, the more you want to reach outside.

P2Ask people who love you, people who are like you, people who have done what you are thinking of doing. Sometimes it is right to go it alone, but I would suggest making it the last step, after you've tried to get council.

P3On the other hand, it is possible to give your power away. Seeking counsel can quietly turn into abdicating to an authority figure. Another person doesn’t get automatic trust, or automatic dismissal.

P4Sometimes you need the support of your peers. In Hearthwork, the concept is that you give each other equal time, warmth, confidentiality, and acceptance of “no” as an answer, and you act for each other as Nurturer and Protector, but not as Guide. Then you reverse roles. Sometimes, with a question asked carefully and at the right time, your peers can help you hear your own Guide more clearly, but they don’t interpret what you experience.

They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it, and our boundary with them still matters, but one day we may find that we have forgiven them.

Appendix H: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens”

P1I speak here from experience.

P2When you’re doing hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca-ing, going through a period of intense grief, praying, or whatever else may alter your consciousness, it’s possible you may run into something that you perceive to be a demon, a jinn, a parasitic energy, or whatever other dark entity or terrifying archetype you may encounter – it may be a voice or an image, and it does n’t just feel like an emotion or a younger part of you, but something that feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, etc.

P3First of all, it doesn’t matter if they’re demons or not. They may be literal demons, for all you know. Or they may be manifestations of your mind, burdens you’re carrying from previous relationships, whatever. What matters is what is the best way to deal with them, so you end up safer, clearer, more loving, more grounded and less hooked.

Start with the room, the body, and basic safety

P1So what do you do when you encounter a demon, or a jinn, or something else that’s bad and intrusive?

P2First of all, do the usual things – make sure you’re not in danger from a medical standpoint, check your environment, check your body, make sure you’re not overstimulating yourself, make sure you’re not opening your mind too much. If you need to, open your eyes, ground yourself in your body and your environment, remove yourself from any bad influence you’re surrounding yourself with, stop stimulating your mind. Don’t go further into whatever it is you’re doing – don’t be curious, don’t try to figure out what it is.

P3Tell yourself, “If this can be integrated in this moment, it’s welcome. If not, it can wait until later. The adult part of me is still here, and my body can return to safety.”

Do not fight from fear

P1Your first instinct may be to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it that you’re more powerful than it is, argue with it, panic, become your own lesser self in fear of it, etc. Some people may want to use traditional prayer or mantras or protection or banishing or exorcism techniques, and those may well work for them. But if you’re fighting it out of fear…

P2It becomes a center of attention if you fear it, and if you hate it you give it a hook in you. (If you’re proud you give it an opponent, and if you panic you give it your nervous system.)

P3So the next time it comes up you can just say, “I see that there is no reason to hate and revile what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to merge with or become what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to obey what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to try to defeat what I am experiencing out of fear. I choose to return my attention to loving awareness.”

A bodily boundary: compassion present, door closed

P1Second, feel free to tell the presence that while you have compassion for it, the door is closed.

P2This is especially a good idea if the presence you’re experiencing seems even the slightest bit hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc. It needs to realize that you don’t welcome it. It’s not really helpful to approach it with the kind of soft, sentimental love that you’d use if you were inviting it to stay for tea, but it can be useful to approach it with love while also making it clear that it needs to respect your boundaries.

P3Sit up, make sure your feet are grounded on the floor, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back a little, open your chest a little, feel the boundary of your torso’s skin, feel the perimeter of your body, and tell the presence, “While I have compassion for you and any suffering you may be experiencing, this suffering needs to go back where it came from. The boundary of my skin is the boundary of an adult now, and you’re not welcome to come inside the house anymore.”

If it might be psychosis or destabilization

P1This is assuming that you are having a symbolic experience of “hostile presences” which responds to grounding and love. It may be that what you are experiencing is actually psychotic or a form of destabilization.

P2If you feel like you are under attack for multiple days at a time, if you are not able to sleep, if you are not able to function normally, if you are hearing voices telling you to do things, if you feel you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, if you feel you are going manic, if you feel you can’t communicate normally, if you feel you can’t distinguish between what you are experiencing symbolically and normal reality, get help immediately. It’s not something to deal with in hypnosis.

ST-11.1, new subheading: The General Rule

P3The General Rule is: if you find that what you're doing is making you more loving, more grounded, more relational, more honest, more functional, then it's probably OK to keep doing it gently. But if what you're doing is making you more Paranoid, sleepless, Grandiose, isolated, scared, or more and more unreal, then DON'T GO DEEPER! GET HELP!

Don’t become an entity hobbyist

P1Finally, some of you may be tempted to make this an area of hobbyism – to become interested in demons or jinns or hostile presences or Unattached Burdens or whatever. I just don’t want you to do that. They all lead to the same thing, which is how to maintain a presence of love without giving up your boundaries, while also making your mind harder to hook.

Appendix I: Sleep hypnosis

P1•For sleep, try using this playlist by Nimja

Appendix J: A practical induction library

P1Practise! Work out in advance which one you want to do and what you want to use it for (pick just one) and whether or not you want to do it at all! Any of these ‘families’ of induction can be done as light inductions, with eyes open, or instead of trance you can just do them as a contact. Once you start an induction, you will want to notice what’s going on (even if nothing changes) and work out what to do next, move, imagine something else, change the sensory channel you’re using, do nothing, stop the induction sequence and do something else… . Whatever you do, make sure you bring yourself fully back to waking at the end of an induction.

P2NB: if you can’t ‘see’ the images you’re trying to visualize, that’s fine, change them into words, rhythm, spatial relations, something to touch or move or just plain ‘knowing’… .

1. Stretch and release

P1Stretch and Release: Work out what will be supporting you, focus on the feeling of support. You can also focus on where one of your hands or feet is. Either actually, or in your imagination, stretch a little bit, either stretching that part of your body slightly or pressing gently down into the support, and then let go of the effort, just relax. See if there is any difference, even if there isn’t. Do this for no more than 3 places on your body. Think of it as ‘releasing’ as you go through the sequence. Which bit of your body, or voice, needs this? What do you need to support it? Bring your body back to normal movement and return.

2. Supported floating

P1Supported Floating: Work out what is supporting you and where your weight is, imagine that the support is holding a tiny bit (1%) more of your effort. It’s like floating but you don’t have to lose contact, or just keep it at the same level, just enough weight/pressure. See what happens, you can fractionate this if you want, perhaps noticing your normal awareness when you breathe in and the support when you breathe out. Tell yourself you are going to do this before you do it. What can you hear more easily now? Bring yourself back to normal feeling of support and return.

3. Rhythmic breath or pulse

P1Rhythmic: Use your breathing or slightly hum in your throat to make a natural rhythm, or tap your finger or listen to sounds outside to make an artificial one. You can even do it by counting to yourself (silently) or with no rhythm at all. Tell yourself you are going to say “here, and here again” over and over, and notice what you pay attention to in between the phrases, then stop saying it. Notice what you become aware of in the first beat – you don’t need to make your mind blank, just notice what comes up. Does it make any words, feelings, needs or actions more clear? Bring back your normal rhythm and return.

4. Unwinding object

P1Unwinding Object: Good for when you have a few different strands to one thing you want to work on. Imagine an object unwinding – maybe some yarn, some bubbles, or some knots that you place beside you. Once you’ve placed them all, give yourself a minute to look at them all, you don’t have to change anything, but you can label them if you need to (just a word or two). How many did you put down? Which one do you need to work on, what does it need – warmth, protection, action? Keep one strand in your attention and put the others somewhere you can see them and return.

5. Sensory journey

P1Sensory Journey: Pay attention to the sounds in the room you’re in and how your body feels, then imagine yourself walking somewhere. Where do you want to go? Listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings as you walk, what do objects feel like if you touch them, what landmarks do you see? When you feel you have enough of your attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where you can talk to whoever you need to (or you can just cut to the chase, if you prefer). Pay attention to something without worrying about what it means. Allow yourself to be curious about what’s going to happen next, but don’t make it a “what are they going to do to you?” kind of thing. When you are ready to finish, imagine yourself walking back the way you came and close the space.

6. Gradual wave

P1Gradual wave: start with a very small neutral area, feel into it a little and then imagine a wave spreading out to a new area that is still ok. Sense into the new area (or continue using the old). See if there is anything different at each step, without claiming it is a medical repair. Does the body want any contact, space, words, other care? Let the mental image go, sense your body, sense your contact points, come back.

7. Care workshop

P1Care workshop: prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come only as close as is welcome. Try to avoid any language that makes you not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that's ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else's function). Have the adult part of you run the show. Goal is to make it "good as you", not to erase history. Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you're an adult now, and come back.

9. No-trance inner contact

P1For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask one clear question and wait, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous: write whatever you get. Deepener: none. Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing. Integration/exit: reality test the autonomous, do one small thing based on it, stop doing it.

This ASCH website , contains information about the usefulness of getting certified in hypnosis, and why it doesn't guarantee competence.
